newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.10 pct.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday set its weekly reverse repurchase operation at a fixed, unchanged 4.10 percent as widely expected by the markets.
A Reuters poll found not one of 12 economists questioned expected the Riksbank to lower the repo rate which is its key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
The Riksbank said the new operation will run from February 12 to February 19.
All primary dealers are invited to leave bids by 0900 GMT on February 11 with the lowest accepted volume 200 million crowns and the highest accepted volume 40 billion crowns.
The Riksbank last lowered the repo rate on December 17. In 1996 it cut the rate from 8.91 percent to 4.10 percent.
The bank's other key interest rates, the deposit and lending rates, that mark out its interest rate corridor, currently stand at 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent.
